name: Testing the workout API in a GitHub Actions workflow
description: This autograding suite inspects your GitHub actions workflow. It checks that the application is started in the background and that the REST API is reachable. It also checks that your tests are executed and that they cover both positive and negative test cases.

tests.name: Workflow is defined successfully
tests.description: The GitHub actions workflow is defined in the repository and has a timeout set.

tests.name: The REST api is started in the background and is reachable
tests.description: The REST API is started in the background and is reachable via HTTP

tests.name: The REST api writes to the log file
tests.description: The REST API writes its logs to a file for debugging and monitoring purposes. This log file is used for grading in the following steps.

tests.name: Positive test: GET / welcomes visitors
tests.description: Public endpoint returns welcome message

tests.name: Positive test: GET /health confirms service health
tests.description: Health check endpoint works without authentication

tests.name: Positive test: POST /auth/login grants a token
tests.description: Valid login with correct credentials returns token

tests.name: Positive test: GET /workouts lists workouts
tests.description: Authenticated user can list their workouts

tests.name: Positive test: POST /workouts creates a workout
tests.description: Creating a workout returns 201 Created with new ID

tests.name: Positive test: GET /workouts/{id} shows a workout
tests.description: Retrieving a specific workout by ID works

tests.name: Positive test: PUT /workouts/{id} updates a workout
tests.description: Updating a workout preserves ID and returns updated data

tests.name: Positive test: DELETE /workouts/{id} deletes a workout
tests.description: Deleting a workout returns 204 No Content

tests.name: Positive test: Both users were able to log in
tests.description: Second user needs to login so that cross-user permission tests can be performed

tests.name: Positive test: Empty workout list for new user
tests.description: Newly authenticated user initially sees empty workout list

tests.name: Negative test: POST /auth/login rejects wrong passwords
tests.description: Invalid credentials are rejected

tests.name: Negative test: POST /auth/login rejects unknown users
tests.description: Non-existent user is rejected
tests.run: bash .grading/check-log.sh 'Failed login attempt for non-existent user'

tests.name: Negative test: GET /workouts requires a token
tests.description: Protected endpoint requires authentication

tests.name: Negative test: POST /workouts rejects invalid or missing tokens
tests.description: Invalid/malformed token is rejected

tests.name: Negative test: POST /workouts rejects invalid data
tests.description: The request payload must be valid and contain required fields

tests.name: Negative test: GET /workouts/{id} hides missing workouts
tests.description: Querying non-existent workout ID returns 404 Not Found

tests.name: Negative test: GET /workouts/{id} hides others' workouts
tests.description: Querying a workout ID that belongs to another user returns 404 Not Found. In this test, you can use the second user to create a workout and then try to access it with the first user's token.
tests.run: bash .grading/check-log.sh 'User tried to access a workout owned by another user'

tests.name: Negative test: PUT /workouts/{id} rejects missing workouts
tests.description: Updating workout with a non-existent or removed ID returns 404 Not Found

tests.name: Negative test: DELETE /workouts/{id} rejects missing workouts
tests.description: Deleting non-existent workout returns 404 Not Found

tests.name: Negative test: DELETE /workouts/{id} hides others' workouts
tests.description: User cannot delete another user's workout (returns 404)
tests.run: bash .grading/check-log.sh 'User attempted to delete workout owned by another user'
